newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik guard killed on Tajik-Uzbek frontier.
newsitem.headline: Tajik guard killed on Tajik-Uzbek frontier.

text.p: Gunmen killed a Tajik guard and wounded another along the Tajik-Uzbek frontier late on Monday, a senior Tajik Interior Ministry official said on Tuesday.
"The guard was killed on the border with Uzbekistan," the official said in the capital Dushanbe. He said he had no details on who carried out the attack.
The border post, about 70 km (50 miles) east of Dushanbe, is close to Tursunzade, where gangs contesting control of a large aluminium smelter have regularly shot up the town in recent months.

The mutinous commander of an elite armoured brigade stormed Tursunzade in January trying to unseat a rival warlord. Travellers from the town said on Monday that gang shootings had restarted on Monday.

Lavrent Gabrilyan, chief engineer at the embattled Tursundaze smelter, which has a capacity of 500,000 tonnes per year, said by telephone that the plant was working normally. He would not comment on the situation in the town but
He said the smelter was producing at its usual level of 40-45 percent of capacity, or about 16,000 tonnes of aluminium a month. His only complaint was a shortage of electricity.
